name: Red Fort, moat and Lahori Gate plaza
notes: The fort itself, the Lahori Gate and the temples across the road come from the landmark registry and OSM, not from this profile.

footpath.surface: broken concrete or grey tile beside a low retaining wall on Netaji Subhash Marg; an open asphalt and stone forecourt 40 to 60 m across in front of the gate; shared with hawkers on the Chandni Chowk side
footpath.kerb: orange and white painted kerb along the moat

lamps.kind: tall twin-arm steel poles at the junction and plaza, single curved-arm poles on the Chandni Chowk side, ground floodlights up the fort wall

kinds: red sandstone rampart with a dry moat 15 to 20 m wide and a 1 m red stone parapet
orange cones for the visitor queue

life.people: visitors of all ages in queues and loose groups, ticket sellers and guards, lemonade and snack sellers at the barricades, rickshaw riders waiting for fares, shopkeepers on the Chandni Chowk side; large crowds on 15 August

road.condition: worn black asphalt with dust, an open plaza with few markings; Netaji Subhash Marg has 3 lanes each way and a kerbed divider

evidence.buildings.mix: sheet red_fort_surroundings 'Buildings': across the road plain white 3 to 4 storey police and administrative blocks and Old Delhi shops; 'Map notes': a parking polygon, not a street. The fort and the temples come from the registry or OSM. Shares are an estimate from the two named types
